title: Branching, commit and push conventions under gates
situation: Cratylus's working conventions said to commit autonomously with no operator approval and that pushing needs the operator's say-so. The first pulled against a gate; the operator, signing off the sign-off-gates story, said pushing a branch or opening a pull request is not a gate, and that the commit convention is the architect's to reword.
decision: Cratylus follows GitHub flow: a short-lived branch per task, merged into dev by pull request; dev merged into main by pull request for release, which is the operator's; a session may run an integration branch ahead of dev for one change and says so. Commit autonomously at natural boundaries between gates, never past one. Pushing a branch and opening a pull request need no say-so. Commit only your own paths, by name; never amend or rewrite shared history.
consequences: The repository's working conventions are reworded to match in the sign-off-gates story.
